source_refs.note: Topic 14.6 (PDF 31); Fig 14.9 is redrawn from the equations. The book's statement that acceleration and displacement differ in phase by pi/2 is corrected in a warning. The check question is added.

blocks.text: The displacement, velocity and acceleration of a body executing S.H.M. can be shown on graphs against time (Fig 14.9).

items: Displacement: x = xo cos(wt) (14.19). The particle has its maximum displacement xo at the extreme positions.
Velocity: its magnitude is xo w sin(wt) (14.20); taking direction into account, v = -xo w sin(wt). The speed is maximum, xo w, at the mean position and zero at the extreme positions.
Acceleration: a = -w^2 x; putting x = xo cos(wt), a = -xo w^2 cos(wt) (14.21). The acceleration is maximum, xo w^2, at the extreme positions and zero at the mean position.

blocks.text: From the graphs: the phase difference between velocity and displacement is pi/2, and the phase difference between acceleration and displacement is pi.

blocks.alt: Three graphs over one period with T/4, T/2, 3T/4 and T marked. Top, blue: x = xo cos(wt), starting at +xo. Middle, green: v = -xo w sin(wt), starting at zero and going negative first. Bottom, red: a = -xo w^2 cos(wt), starting at its most negative value, the mirror image of the displacement graph.
blocks.caption: Displacement, velocity and acceleration in S.H.M. (original graphs after Fig 14.9).
blocks.long_description: Where x is largest, v is zero and a is largest in the opposite direction. Where x is zero, the speed is largest and a is zero.
